kept.q: A ray of light travels from air into a glass block of refractive index 1.5. If the angle of incidence is 30°, calculate the angle of refraction. (sin 30° = 0.5)
kept.explanation: Using n = sin i / sin r, we get sin r = sin i / n = 0.5 / 1.5 = 0.333. Taking the inverse sine gives r = 19.5°.
kept.pidgin: Dem use n = sin i / sin r, so sin r = 0.5/1.5 = 0.333. If you find inverse sine of 0.333, you go get r = 19.5°.

kept.q: A converging (convex) lens has a focal length of 10 cm. An object is placed 15 cm from the lens. Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, calculate the distance of the image from the lens.
kept.explanation: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/10 - 1/15 = (3-2)/30 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm. This means the image forms 30 cm from the lens.
kept.pidgin: 1/v = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm. Na so the image dey form 30 cm from the lens.

kept.q: A convex lens forms a real, inverted image 6 cm high from an object that is 2 cm high. Calculate the linear magnification produced by the lens.
kept.explanation: Linear magnification, m = image height / object height = 6/2 = 3. This tells us the image is 3 times bigger than the object.
kept.pidgin: Magnification, m = image height divide object height = 6/2 = 3. E mean say the image big pass the object by 3 times.

kept.q: The refractive index of a certain type of glass is 1.5. Calculate the critical angle for light travelling from the glass into air. (sin C = 1/n)
kept.explanation: sin C = 1/n = 1/1.5 = 0.667. Taking the inverse sine of 0.667 gives C = 41.8°, which is the critical angle for total internal reflection to just occur.
kept.pidgin: sin C = 1/1.5 = 0.667. If you find inverse sine, you go get C = 41.8°, na so total internal reflection go just begin.

kept.q: In a compound microscope, which of the following best describes the function of the objective lens?
options: It magnifies the final image formed by the eyepiece for direct viewing
It forms a real, inverted and magnified image of the object close to the eyepiece
It reduces the size of the object so it can fit into the eyepiece
It bends light rays from distant objects so they appear closer, like in a telescope
kept.explanation: The objective lens, which is closest to the object, forms a real, inverted and magnified image near the eyepiece; the eyepiece then further magnifies this image for the eye to view. The other options describe the eyepiece or unrelated functions.
kept.pidgin: The objective lens wey dey close to the object go form real, upside-down and bigger image near the eyepiece; na the eyepiece go then magnify am more for eye to see. The other options na the eyepiece work or no relate at all.

q.q: A fisherman standing by the Epe lagoon notices that the water appears to be 1.2 m deep when viewed vertically from above, although the actual depth is 1.6 m. Calculate the refractive index of the lagoon water.
q.explanation: Refractive index n = real depth / apparent depth = 1.6 / 1.2 = 1.33. This is a standard way of finding refractive index using apparent depth.
q.pidgin: n = real depth divide by apparent depth = 1.6/1.2 = 1.33. Na so dem dey calculate refractive index with apparent depth.
